description: Hi! I’m an engineering student passionate about space systems and software development. My goal for this challenge is to build a functional software tool or monitoring system designed to assist astronauts during missions. I am proficient in Python, C++, and C#, dedicated to building functional software solutions for astronaut health and mission safety.
summary:
H.A.S.H (Human Analytics & Smart Health) is an astronaut health-monitoring app that lets crew members assess their own health, understand the risks and act on them without waiting for ground support.

It tracks 14 indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, bone density, sleep, mood, radiation dose, cabin CO₂ and menstrual cycle (shown only for female profiles). Each one links to the five spaceflight hazards: radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, gravity and closed environments. Readings come from typed values, a camera-based pulse estimate and photo logs.

Color-coded cards, live trend charts and a hazard score give an instant read of status. For each indicator the app explains how to measure it in space, why it matters, when to escalate to flight surgeons and what actions to take. It adapts to a spacecraft, station, rover or Mars base, and a period tracker supports women's health. Routine prompts, XP, streaks and badges keep crews engaged.

This matters because communication delays of up to 22 minutes on Mars missions make self-reliant, preventive health care essential for mission safety.
details:
What It Does & How It Works?

H.A.S.H is a self-contained, browser-based astronaut health monitoring, mission-routine, and decision-support web app designed as a training and operational concept (not a certified medical device).

  • Mission & Profile Setup: Opens with an interactive splash screen where the user chooses an astronaut profile (Male or Female) and one of four spaceflight environments: Spacecraft (Mars transit), Space station (low Earth orbit), Pressurized rover (Moon), or Mars surface base, each pre-configured with gravity (0 g, 0.17 g, 0.38 g), one-way signal delay (1 s to 720 s), and baseline radiation dose rates.
  • Hazard-to-Indicator Mapping: Tracks 15 health and environmental indicators (resting heart rate, systolic blood pressure, SpO₂, body temperature, fasting glucose, energy intake, body mass change, vitamin D, bone density T-score, exercise time, sleep, mood/morale, radiation dose rate, cabin CO₂, and days since last period for female profiles). Every indicator links to one or more of the Five Hazards of Spaceflight (space radiation, isolation & confinement, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and closed environment), which can be clicked to filter the dashboard.
  • Interactive Analytics & Drill-Down: Displays an overall readiness score ring, cumulative radiation bar (against an illustrative 600 mSv career reference), and color-coded indicator cards (Good, Watch, Act now) with SVG sparklines. Clicking any card opens a modal with an animated SVG time-series chart, measurement instructions, escalation criteria, environment-specific tips, and customizable thresholds.
  • Camera & Multi-Modal Logging: Supports manual entry, photo logging (meal, rash, ultrasound, or device screens resized on <canvas>), and an experimental rear-camera fingertip pulse estimator that reads red-channel brightness over 15 seconds to estimate BPM.
  • Female-Specific Cycle Tracking: Includes a dedicated period tracker with flow/symptom logging, a 28-day visual grid, cycle-length bar chart, alerts for heavy flow or missed periods, and a planned menstrual suppression toggle.
  • Gamified Daily Routine: Prompts due measurements and daily mission tasks. For example: hydration, resistive exercise, crew check-in, air/CO₂ scrubber checks, storm-shelter drills that award XP, Levels, streaks, and 5 achievement badges, backed by a 30-step Undo (Ctrl+Z) and localStorage persistence.

Benefits:

  • Offline-First & Zero-Backend: Runs completely locally in a single HTML file with localStorage persistence, making it resilient to deep-space blackouts or limited bandwidth.
  • Delay-Aware Guidance: Adapts alert instructions to the current one-way signal delay, prompting immediate ground data sharing in low Earth orbit while prioritizing autonomous onboard self-care protocols on Mars transit or surface missions.
  • Personalized & Sex-Specific: Adjusts reference ranges by biological sex, supports menstrual suppression workflows, and lets flight surgeons customize personal thresholds per indicator.
  • Privacy-Preserving: All health readings and captured photos stay strictly on the user's device.

Intended Impact:

  • Crew Autonomy: Helps astronauts spot subtle physiological and behavioral trends early and understand "why" each metric matters relative to spaceflight hazards when real-time Earth support isn't available.
  • Training & Education: Gives students, analog-mission crews, and researchers an interactive sandbox to simulate how microgravity, radiation, confinement, and closed habitats affect human health over multi-day missions.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software:

  • Languages: Pure HTML5, CSS3 (Custom Properties, Grid, Flexbox, light/dark prefers-color-scheme, prefers-reduced-motion, mobile safe-area-inset support), and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+) with zero external frameworks or build tools.
    • Inline SVG (<animateMotion>, readiness ring, sparklines, and multi-zone trend charts)
    • MediaDevices API (getUserMedia) + Torch constraints for fingertip optical pulse estimation
    • HTML5 <canvas> & FileReader API for client-side photo resizing and JPEG data-URL storage
    • Web Audio API (AudioContext) for synthesized UI, alert, and achievement sound effects
    • Web Storage API (localStorage) for offline state persistence
    • Google Fonts (Sora and Figtree)
  • Hardware: Any smartphone, tablet, or computer with a modern web browser (plus a rear camera and LED flash if using the fingertip pulse estimator or photo log).

How It Is Creative?

  • Single-File Portability: Packs a full mission dashboard, custom SVG charting engine, Web Audio synthesizer, and camera-based pulse detector into one self-contained HTML file.
  • Repurposed Smartphone Optics: Turns a standard phone camera and flash into a makeshift optical pulse sensor using real-time canvas red-channel averaging, detrending, and peak detection.
  • Adaptive UI & Gamification: Dynamically shifts the interface theme by profile and transforms clinical health logging into an engaging daily mission loop with XP, streaks, and audio cues.

Factors Considered:

  • Spaceflight Medical Realities: Modeled around the 5 spaceflight hazards, realistic signal delays, partial/zero gravity environments, and cumulative radiation limits.
  • Biological Sex & Reproductive Health: Accounted for sex-specific cardiovascular reference ranges, menstrual cycle variability under stress/radiation, and planned menstrual suppression.
  • Accessibility & Ergonomics: Included full keyboard navigation (tabindex, Enter/Space, Ctrl+Z undo), ARIA labels/roles, reduced-motion fallbacks, and mobile safe-area padding.
  • Safety & Scope: Designed with clear disclaimers that default thresholds are illustrative and that the tool supports rather than replaces flight-surgeon medical guidance.
